jobs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Rework the existing RONGBOY toy-weapon lineup (image 1) as an art-directable roster of redesigned plush game props. Image 2 is only the world and current needle perspective reference; retain original simple noodle-thin knitting needle silhouette. Exactly eight separate designs, one object per cell, in a clean 4-column × 2-row landscape grid. Same scale conventions and same 3/4 view; entire silhouettes visible, bottoms have comfortable clearance. TOP left to right: (1) original RONGBOY single-barrel compact round cream-felt and terracotta-ring spool pistol from the left object of reference 1, preserve its chubby front ring and side spool knob; (2) distinctly flat and wide garden hose sprayer shotgun, three small cloth-filled muzzle openings in a single horizontal row, short rear handle; (3) large flashlight spotlight cannon with an oversized DEEP circular lamp bezel, a chunky short body, recognizable TOP carry handle, stout rear trigger grip, front hand support and a quilted fabric wrap, deep central toy muzzle and separate ring of warm lamp light; (4) compact dedicated electric-net launcher with closed, boxy wide muzzle enclosing four recessed emitter nodes, no mosquito swatter shape, no racket head, a tiny folding woven light net hanging just beyond the muzzle to clarify what it launches, no lightning bolt by itself. BOTTOM left to right: (5) automatic button launcher inspired by a stapler, with a clear upper hinged press arm and broad lower jaw, avoid literal office stapler and realistic military rifle, easy to read first-person design; (6) original very long thin knitting needle launcher, slender silver knitting needle projecting from the cream fabric and lilac yarn carrier with a round dusty pink needle cap, based on the original game weapon; (7) small fabric jack-in-the-box bomb with chunky squashed patchwork box, lid cracked so the zigzag spring and a tiny sewn clown head can be seen, cheerful cloth not horror; (8) collapsible petal steamer bomb, recognizable overlapping radial steamer leaves, compact muted brass and lavender plush edge band, display partly open with some soft yarn lattice stored inside. Keep solid object designs distinct and angled three-quarters toward front left, only the eight props. No text, no letters, no grid numbers, no people, no hands, no blood, no real military styling, no modern firearm accuracy. Treat everything as fictional toy-like gameplay props for the original RONGBOY felt videogame. Variant A has an old handwritten household workshop feel: visible interlaced dense wool, cream canvas, dusty terracotta, subdued blue-green enamel, aged walnut, dull brass rivets and a few seams only where parts meet. Spotlight cannon is a field lantern from someone's attic, broad vermilion-rubbed metal rim with tiny ivory lining, cream cotton top strap handle with brown wooden core. Garden nozzle flattened oval off-white metal, moss-thyme wrap. Net launcher olive fabric body and recessed mint ceramic nodes in a squared-off rim. Stapler machine gun has terracotta enamel upper press spine and visibly two different thicknesses in the hinge. Natural felt fibers and convincing tactile physical surface. Warm tan studio board with eighth-scale alternating neutral cream linen squares separated by thin light gutters, discrete contact shadows, sophisticated high-end stop-motion maquette reference. Landscape production sheet with 2 rows, four equal columns.

BOTTOM left to right: (5) automatic button launcher inspired by a stapler, with a clear upper hinged press arm and broad lower jaw, avoid literal office stapler and realistic military rifle, easy to read first-person design; (6) original very long thin knitting needle launcher, slender silver knitting needle projecting from the cream fabric and lilac yarn carrier with a round dusty pink needle cap, based on the original game weapon; (7) small fabric jack-in-the-box bomb with chunky squashed patchwork box, lid cracked so the zigzag spring and a tiny sewn clown head can be seen, cheerful cloth not horror; (8) collapsible petal steamer bomb, recognizable overlapping radial steamer leaves, compact muted brass and lavender plush edge band, display partly open with some soft yarn lattice stored inside. Variant B looks like recognisable toys rescued from a primary school activity cupboard and made with felt. Saturated but matte and slightly worn, pale oatmeal felt with seafoam enamel, russet/bricky red, mustard stitches, dark blue canvas. No plastic shine. Feature distinctive alternatives for the four new guns. The spotlight cannon is a blue-green rechargeable garden emergency spotlight with an angular top carry handle and prominent mustard fabric bumper encircling the deep circular front; smaller tube behind. The hose shotgun has a wide rectangular coral-and-mint three-port fan nozzle. The electric-net launcher is compact with a scalloped wide ivory ceramic collar and four inset pale aqua contacts, gauzelike blue net about to unfold. The stapler automatic is a longer low arched seafoam spine over a dark muffled magazine, red pressure pad at rear. Bombs have a little quilted checkerbox clown, and a matte brass-petal silver steamer pod. Highest craft-level detailed 3D material but clean gameplay silhouette and fair scale in each cell. Pale washed robin's-egg and oatmeal neutral presentation background, soft bright studio light, clean no borders other than thin neutral gutters. Large landscape item-sheet.

Use case: stylized-concept. Rework these two original RONGBOY first-person shooter screenshots as a high-end game art direction comparison image of three firing and aiming effects, carrying forward handcrafted wool felt, miniature old toy house rooms, beige stitching, cute round sage-green zombies with crossed button eyes, light felt mittens as player hands. Image 1 guides POV and game identity only, image 2 guides exact play camera hallway and orig thin silver needle launcher. A single landscape image split into exactly THREE equally wide vertical panels with tiny smooth margins. Each panel is an authentic first-person at doll eye height with central surface of play visible, hands and prop lower right, no character behind or above; render tactile wool fibers and believable shadows, keep clear readable target shapes. Panel left: a recognizably retro top-handle flashlight cannon, thick round hollow terracotta/olive muzzle rim and padded cream supports, felt mittens, an actual glowing large warm yarn ball already in the air just in front of a shielded cute button-eye zombie. Its traveling amber ball is a real light source casting a local pool of warm light onto both the wooden floor and close walls, and wrapping the edge of the shield; surrounding dim muted green. One small initial pulse out of the lamp, no sustained flashlight beam and no explosion. Panel center: compact boxy pastel-and-cream net launcher with four recessed emitters, a single electrically glowing blue woven diamond-grid net in midair, expanding forward and draping across TWO nearby separated button-eyed felt zombies inside a stitched classroom, cyan filament a readable flexible open lattice not a solid shape or lightning bolt. No mosquito swatter device. Panel right: same old RONGBOY felt hallway background and needle, strongly magnified circular optic view filling most of this panel, soft dark surround. Inside the circular view, single distant toy zombie now appears FOUR times bigger than outside the circle, clean very thin crosshair, same environment aligns inside/outside. Small tasteful legible exact text near optic edge "+4×" is not needed; render EXACTLY "4×" only. A thin silver tip with muted coral-lilac trim low in foreground. No other lettering, no ammo counters, no logos, no blood, no realistic firearms. This is a game-feel brief, the three outcomes must read right away.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep the 3-panel image, left panel spotlight cannon and all its illumination, right panel 4× circular scope and all lettering, exact widths and original art style. Make a single correction in middle panel, where the net launcher fires the glowing woven blue net as a DETACHED flying projectile that has fully left the gun. Remove all threads or beams or lines extending to the muzzle. Draw a clear, ample gap of bare hallway and floor of at least one muzzle diameter between the projectile and weapon, from just under the leading edge of the hanging diamonds by the zombies to high above the muzzle. Net is already spreading forward around the two original zombies, with a complete open diamond weave and four brighter corner knots. Preserve the two zombie poses, camera, muzzle location, wall, floor and panel border. No electric beam or cable coming out of the launcher. Preserve everything in the first and third panel and their tiny gutters unchanged. This is a fictional toy shooter mockup.

Use case: stylized-concept. Rework original RONGBOY felt shooter room and prop style as a 2×2 landscape game concept storyboard of two DIFFERENT damaging toy grenades, two shots per prop. Reference one is the stitched tiny room and cute green felt button-eye enemies, reference two the tactile prop aesthetic. At top left intact dark terracotta/umber patchwork jack-in-the-box on a worn felt floor, cream nubby zigzag spring raising a comical small clown face just as lid pops. At top right the EXACT SAME jack-in-the-box springs up visibly, a short heavy warm cotton impact at ground level makes one sage green felt zombie tumble backwards and another reel, buttons and a few cotton fibers flying, two small heart-shaped fabric hit markers by enemies to signal damage. The spring and clown and cloth box still recognizable in the middle, no fiery blast. At bottom left CLOSED circular folded steamer bomb sitting on the floor, recognizable overlapping matte brass scalloped flower petals and lilac sewn edge, with a few subtle soft yarn strands just emerging. At bottom right EXACT SAME steamer open like a lotus at the centre of a THIN HORIZONTAL lavender woven ground net, both a short radial mint-lilac cotton pulse and actual visible soft threads catch the legs of two nearby button-eye plush zombies; one flinches at the impact and sheds a few cotton fibers, damage readable; they remain upright visibly tethered, as a different outcome from the knockback above. Same workshop setting in each pair, close gameplay reaction viewpoint behind the orb subject, keep four distinct frames with narrow ivory gutters. Whimsical hand-sewn feel, mature art-directed stylized 3D visual from an elevated close gameplay camera to read props, clearly different two silhouettes and types of hit. No text, no blood, no fire/explosive realism, no unrelated props or HUD, avoid energy fog that obscures the enemies.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep the image exactly as a 2×2 split storyboard in original RONGBOY video game felt toy style. The only edit is to the four floating red heart symbols in the two right-hand tiles (two hearts in upper right, two hearts lower right). Change each intact red felt heart into a clearly fractured two-piece heart pulled apart by a zigzag tear with dark open gap and a tiny cotton tuft pop, visually signifying loss of health. The four little broken hearts must remain equally small, the positions near opponents similar. Keep all toys and hit poses unchanged; top right is a damaging knockback, bottom right is a damaging entanglement. Preserve all rooms, toy weapons, colors and dimensions and every gutter. No added text, numbers or captions, no blood, no other edits.
